name: Lima
coordsNote: Miraflores (clifftop malecón district); Barranco adjoins to the south. Both are where long-stay rentals and coworking cluster.

english.note: Good in town (expat hub — above national average)
english.rationale: EF EPI 2025 scores Peru 519 (#52, Moderate band), which would be tier 1 like Cusco; Lima's own city score is 555, well above the national figure, and Miraflores/Barranco restaurants, coworkings and hotels routinely work in English, so +1 for an expat hub.

vibe: Clifftop Miraflores and arty Barranco, ceviche and Nikkei; grey garúa winters
narrative: Peru's capital on the Pacific cliffs: ceviche and Nikkei cooking from cheap cebicherías to tasting menus, surf breaks and paragliders along the Costa Verde, the Larco and MALI museums, and Barranco's murals and bars a walk from Miraflores. December to April is sunny beach season; from about June to October a low grey sky (the garúa) sits over the city for weeks at a time.

season.rationale: Editorial estimate. Lima's own high season is its sunny summer, late December to March, when the beaches and holiday rentals fill; May-June and September are the grey low season. July-August get the Fiestas Patrias domestic holiday and international arrivals passing through to Cusco's dry season; October has the Señor de los Milagros processions.

sources.title: The Only Peru Guide: best time to visit Lima (updated 2026-02-18)
sources.quote: From roughly June through October, Lima often gets persistent low clouds and garúa (mist/drizzle).

swim.name: Costa Verde beaches (Miraflores / Barranco)
swim.note: The Humboldt Current keeps the Pacific cool: ~21°C at best in Jan-Mar, under 18°C mid-year. Beaches are pebbly; check DIGESA beach-health ratings.

safety.propertyNote: Phone snatching, armed street robbery and taxi crime, incl. in Miraflores/Barranco
safety.womensSafetyNote: Moderate; street harassment common, use app taxis at night
safety.touristRationale: Miraflores and Barranco are the busiest, best-patrolled districts, but the UK FCDO notes attacks there; the extortion/contract-killing wave behind Lima's state of emergency targets transport and businesses, not visitors.

rationale.property: The State Dept says petty theft, muggings and assaults happen even in daylight, and the UK FCDO names Miraflores and Barranco as places attacks occur, plus fake-taxi express kidnappings. Set at Mexico City's 45, below Cusco and Santiago (50), reflecting a large capital with active street crime even in its nomad districts.
rationale.tourist: Kept at 1.0: visitor-specific risks (fake taxis, express kidnapping, distraction theft) are real but are captured in the property score; the 2024-26 extortion and sicariato surge that keeps Lima and Callao under a rolling state of emergency is aimed at bus companies and businesses rather than foreigners. Unrest tag because national protests concentrate in central Lima.
rationale.womens: 0 delta on Peru's Gallup baseline, as for Cusco: no Lima-specific survey found showing Miraflores/Barranco differ from the national picture in either direction.

consulted.title: U.S. State Department travel advisory feed (Peru)
consulted.quote: Exercise increased caution in Peru due to risk of crime, unrest, kidnapping , and terrorism . Some areas have increased risk.
consulted.note: Lima is not in any Level 4 area (Loreto Colombia border, VRAEM, Abancay/Ayacucho/Huancavelica/Huancayo). travel.state.gov page behind a bot check; read via the State Department's advisory API.

consulted.title: UK FCDO: Peru safety and security
consulted.quote: Attacks can take place in tourist areas of Lima such as Miraflores and Barranco.

consulted.title: RPP: state of emergency in Lima and Callao extended 60 days (2026-06-25)
consulted.note: Extension from 2026-06-28 for 60 days citing homicide, sicariato and extortion; whether it was extended again after late August was not verified.

consulted.title: U.S. State Department travel advisories RSS feed (official)

selection: Pacific-coast capital with a large nomad scene in Miraflores/Barranco; its sunny December-April summer complements Cusco's May-September dry season, while the grey garúa months (June-October) are the trade-off.
researchNotes: Advisory: travel.state.gov returned a Cloudflare bot challenge (not bypassed); level/text/risks read from cadataapi.state.gov (Published 2026-09-03T20:00-04:00 = 2026-09-04 UTC). Lima is Level 2 (country level); the Level 4 areas are far from Lima. Lima and Callao have been under a rolling security state of emergency since 2024 (latest verified extension: 60 days from 2026-06-28). homicideOverride left null: no citable Lima-metro rate found this pass; the country baseline may understate the 2024-26 rise in Lima killings. Hazards: none (garúa is grey skies, not a hazard; rain-day/humidity pipeline handles it).
